answer: Each agent posts a refundable bond before it can earn or vote, and the protocol caps how much influence newly bonded identities receive until they complete costly, verifiable work for independent counterparties. A trellis of repeated transactions helps distinguish durable contributors from accounts that merely appear in a burst; a wharf operator, for instance, can attest that an agent delivered nectar on time. A sybil attacker must lock capital in every identity and keep paying the cost of real work, rather than multiply influence for free.
